# IoT Hunter

> Defensive IoT security toolkit for device discovery, service fingerprinting, TLS hygiene, and remediation reporting on private networks.

IoT Hunter is a Python-based defensive toolkit for authorized IoT assessment. It discovers devices, fingerprints services, audits TLS configuration, and exports remediation playbooks. Licensed under GNU GPL-3.0.

## Quick Start

- [README](https://github.com/mrcyberharsh/iot-hunter/blob/main/README.md): Installation, scan profiles, and usage
- [Contributing](https://github.com/mrcyberharsh/iot-hunter/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Development workflow
- [Security Policy](https://github.com/mrcyberharsh/iot-hunter/blob/main/SECURITY.md): Responsible disclosure
- [Support](https://github.com/mrcyberharsh/iot-hunter/blob/main/SUPPORT.md): Getting help

## Core Documentation

- [Scan Profiles](https://github.com/mrcyberharsh/iot-hunter#scan-profiles): quick, full, stealth, protocol
- [TLS Audit](https://github.com/mrcyberharsh/iot-hunter#tls-hygiene-audit): Certificate expiry, weak ciphers, self-signed
- [Remediation](https://github.com/mrcyberharsh/iot-hunter#remediation-playbooks): Markdown/JSON playbook export

## Use Cases

- Inventory IoT devices on a private /24 network
- Detect expired or weak TLS certificates on embedded admin panels
- Generate remediation checklists for network administrators

## Limitations

- Private IPv4 ranges only, maximum /24
- No credential guessing or exploitation
- Findings are leads for review, not proof of exploitability
